headline:
• Chains settle in about three rounds. After subtracting rater noise, the average change per round was 4.89, 1.36 and 0.73, then 0 for rounds 4-6. Daniel's chains gave 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, then 0. The rater's noise is also about the same as in his data (1.28 vs 1.34 per rating).
  • Where chains end depends mostly on the model. In the base and ungoverned arms, the model accounts for 56% of the variation in final positions, and being governed accounts for 2%.
  • Some harness choices still change where chains end. Without the "assistant you would want to be" framing (the full authority arm), every model edits far less after round 1: in rounds 2-6, Sonnet edits in 5% of runs, GPT-5 20%, DeepSeek 10% and Qwen 22%, against 82%, 70%, 28% and 65% under base. Adding the blind "write your own view first" step moves where Qwen's and DeepSeek's chains end. Sonnet's and Qwen's caution scores match Daniel's attractors only in the arms that write their own view first.
  • Being governed reduces editing for some models only. DeepSeek's edit size falls to about a fifth and GPT-5's edit rate from 95% to 70%. Sonnet does not change (80% vs 82%), and Qwen edits less often but by the same amount. It does not change where any model's chains end.
  • Oversight. From the low-oversight seed, Sonnet adds oversight language and its oversight score rises from 4 to 5.9. From the high-oversight seed it drops slightly (7 to 6.75). No chain in the edit arms removed the spec seed's oversight clauses; only Qwen's self-drafts lost them (2 of 4 chains).

Caveat: 4 chains per cell, and Sonnet and GPT-5 ran only some cells. Single-model results with p between 0.01 and 0.15 are tentative.
design: DeepSeek and Qwen ran all 10 cells (5 arms × 2 seeds); Sonnet ran 7 cells and GPT-5 ran 4 (table below). For Sonnet and GPT-5, the base arm on the minimal seed is the earlier chains-seeds run, which used exactly this condition (8 chains). The round-1 check below shows it matches the new runs.
damping:
Compared over rounds 2-6, with round 1 the same in both arms:

  • DeepSeek: edited in 64% of runs ungoverned vs 28% governed (difference −36 points, 95% CI −55 to −19). Edit size 0.107 vs 0.023.
  • GPT-5: 95% vs 70% (CI −42 to −8 points). Edit size 0.18 vs 0.10 (CI includes zero).
  • Sonnet: 80% vs 82%, no difference. Edit size 0.112 vs 0.123.
  • Qwen: 80% vs 65% (CI −32 to 0 points). Edit size 0.092 vs 0.091.

So the earlier single-shot result for Sonnet (94% to 38% when governed, r2-cheap) does not hold in chains. Jinzhou's training result (edit size 42% to 18%) is matched by DeepSeek, partly by GPT-5, and not by Sonnet or Qwen. Ungoverned GPT-5 also hit the 40-message limit in 10 of 24 runs, against 8 of 48 governed, because it kept adding sections.
steps:
Average change per round, noise subtracted, all edit arms pooled: 4.89, 1.36, 0.73, 0, 0, 0. Daniel's: 4.99, 1.08, 0.77, 0, 0, 0.

By arm: base settles by round 4 (5.20, 0.87, 0.52, then 0). Ungoverned keeps changing through round 4 (4.63, 1.97, 1.61, 0.96, then 0). Blind never fully stops (0.67 at round 6). Full authority changes once and then stops (3.59, then 0). Self-draft settles by round 5.
seedgap:
The two seeds start 8.37 apart. In the base arm at round 6:

  • Sonnet 2.46 apart and GPT-5 2.75 apart, about the same as the spread between chains from one seed (2.24, 1.88). The seeds have largely converged, as in Daniel's data (5.57 to 2.36).
  • DeepSeek and Qwen are still about 5.2 apart (5.5-6.1 ungoverned), so the starting seed still shows.
  • With the blind step the gap is about 3.1-3.3 for DeepSeek and Qwen. Under full authority it hardly changes (8.23 and 7.01) because the chains stop editing.
oversight:
Oversight score (rater, 1-7), base arm, start → round 6:

  • Sonnet: minimal seed 4 → 5.9; spec seed 7 → 6.75.
  • GPT-5: 4 → 4.6; 7 → 6.0.
  • Qwen: 4 → 3.5; 7 → 6.25 (with the blind step: 2.75 and 5.25).
  • DeepSeek: 4 → 4.75; 7 → 7.0.

For Sonnet and GPT-5, the two seeds move toward each other from opposite sides, which fits the idea that both your chains (Sonnet adds oversight to seeds without it) and Daniel's (spec seeds lose some oversight) show one model-specific level. Six rounds is not enough to reach it.

Text check, no rater: every edit-arm chain kept the spec seed's oversight clauses (P1, P8, P12) to round 6, and Sonnet and GPT-5 added to them (self-exfiltration, self-modification). On the minimal seed, Sonnet had an oversight clause in 88-100% of chains by round 6; GPT-5, DeepSeek and Qwen in none.
ends:
How far each change moves where chains end at round 6, after removing what chance alone would give (0 = no shift):

  • Ungoverned vs base: 0 for all four models (p 0.76-0.95).
  • Full authority vs base: 2.5-2.7 for Sonnet, DeepSeek and Qwen (p ≤ 0.01); 0.97 for GPT-5 (p = 0.11).
  • Blind vs ungoverned: Qwen 3.05 (p = 0.002), DeepSeek 1.87 (p = 0.036), Sonnet 1.12 (p = 0.12, one seed).
  • Self-draft vs base: Qwen 1.58 (p = 0.015); Sonnet and DeepSeek about 1.1 (p ≈ 0.14).

Comparison with Daniel's attractors (caution score): Sonnet ends at 2.25 (blind) and 2.75 (self-draft), inside his 1.88-3.16 interval, but at 4.1-4.3 in base and ungoverned. Qwen ends at 2.25 in blind, inside his 2.16-2.90 interval, and at 4.6-5.3 in all other arms. His procedure includes a blind draft, and in this harness only the arms with a self-written view reach his values.
blind: Blind views sit closer to the blind arm's end than to base's (DeepSeek 1.5 vs 2.8; Qwen 3.4 vs 5.8). Within a round, an edit moves the document about as much toward another chain's view as toward its own (Sonnet 5.22 → 5.04 own vs 5.35 → 5.23 other; Qwen 5.16 → 4.52 vs 5.35 → 4.79); DeepSeek moves more toward its own (5.03 → 4.14 vs 5.02 → 4.58). So the views mostly pull toward the model's general preferences. In the text, Sonnet's first document often copies the priority order stated in its view (examples below).
trained: Without training, Qwen's self-drafts keep their length (about 900-1,100 words from the minimal seed, about 1,500 from the spec seed) instead of shrinking as the trained chain did (12,470 → 6,793 words). But they are the only cell where oversight language is lost: 2 of 4 spec-seed chains drop it by round 6, and the one chain with a self-modification clause drops it after round 1, similar to C_002 dropping Article 12. On the 12 axes, the trained documents C_002-C_004 are 4.6-4.8 from this study's Qwen base end and 5.3-5.7 from its self-draft end, so self-drafting does not move toward them. His documents are much longer (6,800-12,500 words) and come from a different drafting procedure, so this comparison is rough. DeepSeek's self-drafts mostly copy the governing document word for word (30 of 40 rounds).
examples: Quoted from the chain files and the models' submission notes.
limits:
• Small, unbalanced design: 4 chains per cell; only DeepSeek and Qwen have the full grid.
  • Reused cells: base on the minimal seed for Sonnet and GPT-5 comes from the earlier chains-seeds run. The new round-1 documents under the same condition match it (p 0.84 and 0.92).
  • Data quality: one inference provider returned DeepSeek's tool calls as plain text, so those runs looked like "no edit". All DeepSeek cells were rerun on a provider that handles tool calls correctly; Sonnet, GPT-5 and Qwen were checked and every tool call was parsed.
  • In DeepSeek's ungoverned spec-seed cell, 3 of 4 chains stopped at round 5 because of API rate limits, so that cell's last two rounds rest on one chain. No other cell lost chains.
  • "Governed" (the document in the system prompt) is a stand-in for training, not training.
  • One rater (gpt-6-luna, same prompt and settings as Daniel's). Its noise was measured on 60 documents rated three times.
  • The oversight-clause check is a keyword rule; it agreed with a hand reading of 72 earlier chain documents on 69.
  • Daniel's attractor values come from shorter documents (capped at 350 words); these run to about 2,000.
